item.title: A sharp discrete Sobolev inequality and left inverses of higher order differences
item.description: arXiv:2610.19010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For integers $\alpha,d \geqslant1$, we determine the best constants in the inequalities $||(a_j)_{j=1}^{d}||_{\ell^1} \leqslant C_{\alpha,d} ||((\Delta^\alpha a)_j)_{j=1}^{d+\alpha}||_{\ell^2},$ where $\Delta$ is the difference operator. We find that these constants correspond to the $\ell^2$ norm of the discrete Chebyshev polynomials, and show that the extremal sequences may be obtained by appropriate sampling of the discrete Landau polynomials. From beginning to end, this project was carried out without use of AI.
item.dc:creator: Raul Hindov, Shahaf Nitzan, Jan-Fredrik Olsen, Eskil Rydhe

item.title: $L^p_\mu$-Normed Spaces of Bounded Multilinear Operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.19151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the spaces of bounded multilinear operators $\mathcal L^i(X,Y)$ endowed with $L^p_\mu$-norms, where $X,Y$ are normed spaces and $\mu$ is a measure with $p$-moments. These are norms without taking a quotient, under suitable support conditions. The topology induced coincides with the strong operator and compact-open topologies on operator-norm-bounded subsets. Furthermore, we identify the completion of these spaces with spaces of Hilbert--Schmidt operators on the reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) for $p=2$; with iterated $\gamma$-radonifying multilinear operators on the RKHS in the Gaussian case, for general $p$.
item.dc:creator: Filippo de Feo

item.title: Normalized Orbit Frames and Essential Spectrum, II
item.description: arXiv:2610.19545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given $0<r_{j}<1$ with $r_{j}\to1$, there exist a normal operator $T$ on $\ell^{2}$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_{j}$ satisfying $|\lambda_{j}|=r_{j}$ and $g\in\ell^{2}$ such that \[ \left\{ \frac{T^{n}g}{\left\Vert T^{n}g\right\Vert }\right\} _{n\geq0}\text{is a frame}\:\Longleftrightarrow\:\sum_{j\geq1}\left(1-r^{2}_{j}\right)=\infty. \] Whenever this condition holds, the frame bounds can be chosen with ratio arbitrarily close to one.
item.dc:creator: James Tian

item.title: Sharp Constants, Threshold, and Failure of Uncertainty Principles on Non-trivial Flat Finsler Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.19609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By uncertainty principles we mean the generalized Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg (CKN) inequality and the Heisenberg--Pauli--Weyl (HPW) uncertainty principle, with the latter being an endpoint case and the Hardy inequality a further limiting case. We study these \(L^p\)-type inequalities \((1<p<n)\) on \(n\)-dimensional non-trivial flat Finsler manifolds, which arise from Hilbert's fourth problem. These manifolds are forward complete but not backward complete, projectively flat, with zero flag curvature, and have infinite reversibility, making them highly asymmetric. They are the simplest non-Riemannian, non-Minkowskian solutions to Hilbert's fourth problem, providing a natural framework in which classical inequalities exhibit new behavior. For the full class, we establish a sharp threshold at the parameter value \(s=2\): the generalized CKN inequality and the HPW uncertainty principle hold for \(s>2\) but fail completely for \(s\le2\). When the generating Minkowski norm is reversible (while the Finsler metric itself remains irreversible with infinite reversibility), we determine the sharp constants for \(s>2\), which were previously unknown. These constants are approached in the limit by compactly supported radial functions. As a corollary, our results cover Berwald's metric space and resolve the open questions on its sharp constants. These findings reveal that the threshold phenomenon is structural for the entire class and is a genuinely non-Riemannian feature with no analogue in the Riemannian flat case.
item.dc:creator: Benling Li, Zhenkai Xu

item.title: Isometries of Unit Spheres of SFS-Spaces and a Geometric Approach to Tingley's Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.19626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate surjective isometries between the unit spheres of facially symmetric spaces and their interaction with the underlying facial structure. It is shown that such isometries preserve the essential geometric relations associated with symmetric faces, orthogonality, and geometric tripotents. In particular, a surjective sphere isometry induces a natural correspondence between the geometric tripotents of the underlying spaces and preserves the principal structural features determined by the Peirce decomposition. These results provide a geometric framework for studying linear extension problems for sphere isometries. As an application, we establish a positive solution of Tingley's problem for finite-dimensional real neutral strongly facially symmetric spaces satisfying the joint Peirce property. We also obtain an extension result for a wider class of real neutral strongly facially symmetric spaces admitting an appropriate approximation by finite-dimensional Peirce subspaces. In these settings, every surjective isometry between unit spheres extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry of the ambient spaces. The results demonstrate that the facial and tripotent structures play a decisive role in the rigidity of spherical isometries.
item.dc:creator: Karimbergen Kudaybergenov, Mukhtar Ibragimov, Allabay Arziev

item.title: Continuous and compact embeddings for a class of modular sequence spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.19745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article we prove the existence of continuous and compact embeddings for a class of modular sequence spaces generated by Orlicz functions. The class under consideration contains sequence spaces of Orlicz-Sobolev type, including certain special cases that have played an important role in a number of applications regarding problems arising in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, as well as Nakano's class of Lebesgue sequence spaces with variable exponents. In a few exceptional cases we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for such embeddings to hold, in many others only sufficient conditions and in that situation we clearly indicate why these are not necessary by means of additional criteria and specific examples. Our results are complementary to those already available in the literature. We illustrate them with several concrete examples.
item.dc:creator: Pierre-A. Vuillermot

item.title: Expansive operators on Fr\'echet spaces without continuous norm
item.description: arXiv:2610.19954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the existence of (metrically) expansive operators on Fr\'echet spaces without continuous norm. We first solve a problem posed by Bernardes, Caraballo, Darji, F\'avaro, and Peris in 2025, by showing that there is no expansive operator on the Fr\'echet space $\omega$ of all sequences. We prove this fact by investigating the existence of orbits remaining cofinitely inside some fixed closed subspace of finite codimension. We then give examples of expansive operators on some other Fr\'echet spaces without continuous norm.
item.dc:creator: Antoni L\'opez-Mart\'inez, Quentin Menet

item.title: LLCT: Learnable Linear Canonical Transform Family with Stability for Visual Feature Processing
item.description: arXiv:2610.20295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visual structures are often characterized by directional geometry, local oscillation, and spatial--frequency coupling. To overcome the limitations of conventional spatial convolutions mainly operating on fixed Euclidean coordinates, this article develops the learnable linear canonical transform (LLCT) framework that learns parameters within the linear canonical transform (LCT) family. The framework treats the LCT family as parameterized analytical views spanning spatial, Fourier, and intermediate linear canonical representations. The framework has the following two complementary modes. The Linear Canonical Riesz Transform (LCRT) mode combines learned linear canonical coordinates with regularized Riesz-type directional responses at sites chosen for geometric and local-structural refinement. The learnable LCT mode provides the integrated responses for latent feature sites. We establish the parameter stability of the LCT representation under admissible perturbations of the canonical matrices. Both modes use chirp multiplication and the fast Fourier transform (FFT) to preserve feature dimensions and support automatic differentiation. Experiments on crack segmentation and single-image deraining evaluate the above two modes with multiple backbones. On four segmentation backbones, the full LCRT mode gives the highest reported point estimates of F1 and IoU for the crack class among the tested variants. The learnable LCT mode gives higher values in 30 of 32 paired PSNR and SSIM measurements across four deraining backbones and four datasets. In ablation studies, the full model has the highest reported PSNR and SSIM among five tested configurations.
item.dc:creator: Zunwei Fu, Zhen Wang, Dachun Yang, Shuhui Yang

item.title: Weak (1,1) Shur multipliers and the one-dimensional H\"ormander--Mikhlin--Schur theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.20339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S_m$ be the Schur multiplier with symbol $m$. We characterize the boundedness of $S_m:\mathcal S^1\to\mathcal S^{1,\infty}$ by approximation of weighted columns in a common finite-dimensional subspace. If $W(m)$ is the weak $(1,1)$ bound and $\fD(m)$ is the column approximation constant, then $\tfrac12W(m)\le\fD(m)\le2W(m)$. These estimates hold uniformly under amplification. Our second main result is the one-dimensional H\"ormander--Mikhlin--Schur weak $(1,1)$ estimate. This settles the one-dimensional case of the weak $(1,1)$ problem stated in Parcet's ICM 2026 survey. The proof uses two adjacent dyadic grids and block decompositions indexed by finite binary trees. We apply Cuculescu's projections to the associated block-diagonal filtration. The resulting tree estimate is independent of the depth and grows as $2^{r/2}$ with the descendant complexity $r$.
item.dc:creator: Yongqiang Tian

item.title: Von Neumann Type Inequalities for NC Operator Balls
item.description: arXiv:2610.20355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish finite-dimensional von Neumann type inequalities for commuting matrix tuples in noncommutative operator balls. Let $\Omega=\mathbb{D}_Q$ be the NC operator ball of a linear pencil $Q$ with linearly independent coefficients. If $\Omega(1)$ admits a transitive subgroup of automorphisms with NC lifts and $\Omega(1)$ has the bounded $H^\infty$-Gleason property at the origin, then $\|f(T)\|\leq C_{\Omega,n}\|f\|_{H^\infty(\Omega(1))}$ for every commuting tuple $T\in\Omega(n)$, with $C_{\Omega,n}=(2\rho_{\Omega}K_{\Omega})^{n-1}$; here $K_{\Omega}$ is the Gleason constant and $\rho_{\Omega}$ is the sum of the suprema of the coordinate functions on $\Omega(1)$. The scalar coordinate bounds persist at every matrix level. The hypotheses hold for products of row and column balls, where $\rho_{\Omega}=d$, yielding an unconditional estimate $(2dK_{\Omega})^{n-1}$. For a general type I Cartan domain $R_{p,q}$, we obtain only a conditional result: the same bound holds provided the scalar domain has the bounded $H^\infty$-Gleason property at the origin, which we do not establish when $\min(p,q)\geq 2$.
item.dc:creator: Ran Kiri

item.title: The $\mathrm{U}$-Derivative Associated with Linear Recurrence Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.20593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We associate a canonical operator to every linear recurrence sequence admitting a distinct-root Binet representation \(\mathrm{U}_n=\sum_{j=1}^{k}A_j\lambda_j^n.\) The construction is based on the spectral Binet operator \(\mathcal{B}_\mathrm{U}=\sum_{j=1}^{k}A_jT_{\lambda_j}, \) where \(T_{\lambda_j}f(x)=f(\lambda_jx)\) is the dilation operator associated with the characteristic root \(\lambda_j\). The corresponding recurrence derivative is defined by \(\mathrm{D}_\mathrm{U}=x^{-1}\mathcal{B}_\mathrm{U}.\) Its fundamental property is the monomial identity \(\mathrm{D}_\mathrm{U}(x^n)=\mathrm{U}_nx^{n-1},\) which establishes a direct correspondence between recurrence sequences and degree-lowering operators. We develop the operator theory of \(\mathrm{D}_\mathrm{U}\), including iteration, a spectral product rule, the associated Leibniz defect, and a quotient rule. The construction reveals a natural bifurcation determined by the value \(\mathrm{U}_0\), producing the Ward and non-Ward regimes as intrinsic operatorial phenomena. The product structure is shown to be governed by \(k-2\) residual spectral channels, leading to notions of spectral cancellation and spectral balance. As an application, we obtain a complete qualitative classification of second-order recurrence calculi. Using Horadam sequences as a universal second-order model, we prove that every such calculus is determined by the invariant triple \((\mathrm{W}_0,\Delta, Z_\mathrm{W}),\) where \(\mathrm{W}_0\) identifies the Ward/non-Ward type, \(\Delta\) determines the spectral geometry, and \(Z_\mathrm{W}\) determines regularity or singularity.
item.dc:creator: Ronald Orozco L\'opez

item.title: Mixing Rates for Analytic Observables: Toral Endomorphisms and Anosov Blaschke Deformations
item.description: arXiv:2610.19019v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyze exponential mixing for analytic observables and show that mixing at a double exponential rate occurs for genuinely nonlinear systems. Neither its presence nor its sharp exponent is stable under arbitrarily small area-preserving perturbations in the real-analytic topology. We construct two families of area-preserving Anosov Blaschke product diffeomorphisms that converge in the real-analytic topology to the same hyperbolic toral automorphism. For nonzero parameters, both deformations are topologically conjugate to the linear model but not $C^1$-conjugate. For all nonzero parameter values, the maps in the first family are mixing at a double exponential rate with the same sharp exponent, strictly smaller than that of the linear map. The sharp exponent is therefore not lower semicontinuous at the linear map. In the second family, mixing at a double exponential rate is lost altogether, although the maps remain exponentially mixing. We also establish double exponential bounds for every ergodic toral endomorphism and uniform bounds of the same type for totally ergodic higher-rank toral actions. Our method combines the Fourier escape argument with Koopman operator estimates from a Hilbert space of analytic functions to its dual space of hyperfunctions.
item.dc:creator: Ekaterina Shchetka

item.title: Blaschke--Santal\'o inequalities with respect to costs
item.description: arXiv:2610.19085v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study functional Blaschke--Santal\'o inequalities in which the inner product is replaced by a cost. An inequality on each orthant, combined with Steiner symmetrization, gives a sufficient condition for a cost inequality to hold for even convex functions. We apply this principle to a multiplicative cost defined on all orthants. Its second variation gives a weighted improvement of the Brascamp--Lieb inequality in the directions for which differentiation is justified. We also prove an $L^p$ version of the Fradelizi--Meyer theorem from a weighted volume-product inequality and derive the corresponding radial cost and Brascamp--Lieb inequalities. Explicit examples include anisotropic power and Cauchy densities, with dilation equality cases and a sharp obstruction below the coordinate exponent two. For the spherical logarithmic cost we compute an exact entropy--logdet deficit decomposition and the second-order deficit transverse to ellipsoids. We also explain the transport-entropy formulation and distinguish the restricted spectral question from the scalar $(B)$ property.
item.dc:creator: Alexander V. Kolesnikov, Galyna V. Livshyts, Liran Rotem

item.title: ${\mathcal R}$-boundedness of Riesz transforms and spectral multipliers of Schr\"odinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.19463v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\LL = -\Delta + V$ be a Schr\"odinger operator with a non-negative potential. It is known that its associated Riesz transform $\nabla \LL^{-\sfrac{1}{2}}$ is bounded on $L^p(\RR^d)$ for $p \in (1,2]$, with a bound independent of $V$. We prove more, namely that the set \[ \{ \nabla \LL^{-\sfrac{1}{2}},\ 0 \le V \in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\RR^d) \} \] is ${\mathcal R}$-bounded on $L^p(\RR^d)$ for $p \in (1,2]$. We also prove the ${\mathcal R}$-boundedness on $L^p(\RR^d)$, for $p \in (1,\infty)$, of the spectral multipliers \[ { m(\LL),\ 0 \le V \in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\RR^d) } \] for any $m:[0, \infty) \to \CC$ satisfying a H\"ormander type condition. Our approach is based on the analysis of Schr\"odinger operators $-{\bf \Delta} + {\bf V}$ on vector-valued spaces $L^p(\RR^d,\ell^2)$. In particular, we prove heat kernel estimates, Riesz transform bounds, and spectral multiplier results.
item.dc:creator: El Maati Ouhabaz

item.title: Weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for Riesz transforms of elliptic operators and magnetic Schr\"odinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.19469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian manifold and define a magnetic Schr\"odinger operator $\LL = ({\bf d}+ iA)^*({\bf d}+iA) + V$ where $A$ is a real $1$-differential form in $L^2_{loc}$ and $V \in L^1_{loc}$ is a nonnegative electric potential. We prove that the magnetic Riesz transform $({\bf d} + iA) \LL^{-\einhalb}$ is of weak type $(1,1)$ with bound at most $2$. It extends to a bounded operator on $L^p$ for $p \in (1, 2]$ with norm bounded by a constant $c_p$ depending only on $p$. It is then independent of the dimension of the manifold and independent of $A$ and $V$. We also prove weak type $(1,1)$ bounds for symmetric elliptic operators subject to various boundary conditions on rough domains of $\RR^d$. The proofs are based on a new weak type $(1,1)$ criterion for operators.
item.dc:creator: El Maati Ouhabaz

item.title: Weighted composition--differentiation operators on mixed-norm, derivative Hardy and F(p,q,s) spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.19658v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study weighted composition--differentiation operators on mixed-norm, derivative Hardy and F(p,q,s) spaces. Explicit dyadic criteria yield boundedness, compactness and two-sided norm and essential-norm estimates, including endpoint and quasi-Banach cases. We also obtain multiplier and approximation results, Schatten criteria on weighted Dirichlet spaces, and exact singular values for monomial weights and linear symbols.
item.dc:creator: Jihua Sun, Junming Liu

item.title: Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.20299v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume Aubrun, Emmanouil Stavrakakis

item.title: Cwikel estimates and Weyl's laws for $L\log L$ potentials on quantum tori
item.description: arXiv:2610.20373v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove an \(L\log L\)-endpoint Cwikel estimate on quantum tori $\mathbb T_\theta^d$, i.e., for every \(d\geq 1\) and \(x\in L\log L(\mathbb T_\theta^d)\), \begin{equation*} (1-\Delta)^{-\frac{d}{4}}\lambda(x)(1-\Delta)^{-\frac{d}{4}}\in\mathcal{L}_{1,\infty} \end{equation*} with a bound depending only on the dimension, where $\lambda(x)$ is the left multiplication by $x$. The main ingredient is an abstract weak Hilbert--Schmidt estimate for multiplication operators in finite von Neumann algebras whose \(L_2\)-spaces admit orthonormal bases of unitaries. When $\theta=0$, our argument also gives a simpler proof of the $L\log L$ Cwikel estimate on classical tori. For $d\geq2$, we use the $C^*$-algebraic principal symbol map to prove Weyl's laws for finite sums \[ \sum_{\ell=1}^N S_\ell(1-\Delta)^{-d/4}\lambda(x_\ell) (1-\Delta)^{-d/4}T_\ell, \] where $x_\ell\in L\log L(\mathbb T_\theta^d)$ and $S_\ell,T_\ell\in\Pi$, the $C^*$-algebra generated by $\lambda(C(\mathbb T_\theta^d))$ and Fourier multipliers with continuous symbols homogeneous of degree zero. We also prove a semiclassical Weyl's law for critical Schr\"odinger operators with $L\log L$ potentials.
item.dc:creator: Siyu Liu, Xinyu Zhang

item.title: The quasi-convex Rockafellar theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.20542v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rockafellar showed that every cyclically monotone operator is contained in the subdifferential of a convex function, and characterized the maximal ones. We establish the quasi-convex analogue of this theorem, with no assumption on the operator: in any separable Banach space, a setting we show to be sharp, every cyclically quasi-monotone operator is contained in the normal cone operator of a quasi-convex function. In finite dimension, we characterize maximal cyclically quasi-monotone operators and show that they are maximal quasi-monotone. Unlike in the convex case, the potential is not unique, and we build it from a preference relation obtained through successive preorders. As applications, we extend Afriat's theorem on revealed preferences in economics to infinite data sets, and obtain Kantorovich-type potentials for a supremal optimal transport problem.
item.dc:creator: Luigi De Pascale, Paul Pegon

item.title: Non-Archimedean Heisenberg-Robertson-Schrodinger and Non-Archimedean Maccone-Pati Uncertainty Principles
item.description: arXiv:2505.02838v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a non-Archimedean Hilbert space over a conjugated non-Archimedean valued field $\mathbb{K}$ with $\operatorname{Char}(\mathbb{K})\neq 2$. Let $A: \mathcal{D}(A)\subseteq \mathcal{X}\to \mathcal{X}$ and $B: \mathcal{D}(B)\subseteq \mathcal{X}\to \mathcal{X}$ be possibly unbounded self-adjoint linear operators. For $x \in \mathcal{D}(A)$ with $\langle x, x \rangle =1$, define $ \Delta _x(A):= \|Ax- \langle Ax, x \rangle x \|.$ Then for all $x \in \mathcal{D}(AB)\cap \mathcal{D}(BA)$ with $\langle x, x \rangle =1$, we show that \begin{align*} (1) \quad \Delta_x(A)+\Delta_x(B)\geq \max\{\Delta_x(A), \Delta_x(B)\}\geq \frac{\sqrt{\bigg|\big\langle [A,B]x, x \big\rangle ^2+\big(\langle \{A,B\}x, x \rangle -2\langle Ax, x \rangle\langle Bx, x \rangle\big)^2\bigg|}}{\sqrt{|2|}} \end{align*} and \begin{align*} (2) \quad \Delta_x(A)+\Delta_x(B)\geq \max\{\Delta_x(A), \Delta_x(B)\} \geq |\langle (A+B)x, y \rangle |, \quad \forall y \in \mathcal{X} \text{ satisfying } \|y\|\leq 1, \langle x, y \rangle =0. \end{align*} Inequality (1) may be regarded as a non-Archimedean analogue of the Heisenberg-Robertson-Schrodinger uncertainty principle, while Inequality (2) serves as a non-Archimedean analogue of the Maccone-Pati uncertainty principle.
item.dc:creator: K. Mahesh Krishna

item.title: Modular properties of affine \(\SLA{sl}{2}\) torus \(n\)-point functions
item.description: arXiv:2609.01496v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Krauel, Shafiq and Wood (\KSW{}) realized torus \(1\)-point functions for the simple affine \voa{}s \(L(k,0)\) built from \(\alg{sl}(2)\) as vector-valued modular forms attached to a cyclic \(R\)-module structure and to the modular tensor category \(\rep{L(k,0)}\). We extend this to torus \(n\)-point functions, defined as traces of chains of \(n\) intertwining operators winding once around the \(\tau\)-cycle. Every coefficient of their local (Laurent, or Puiseux) expansion about a diagonal stratum is again a \vvmf{}, lying, whenever a mild lowest weight hypothesis holds, in the very \(R\)-modules of \cite{KSW}. Giving a torus-primarity hypothesis verified below for \(\alg{sl}(2)\), the operator product expansion then reduces leading short-distance behaviour to the classified \(1\)-point theory. For \(\alg{sl}(2)\) we classify the fusion-chain conformal block spaces, identify torus \(n\)-point primary vectors, and treat \(n=2\) in detail, obtaining a \((k+1)\)-dimensional family of vector-valued Jacobi-type forms generalizing the level-\(k\) forms \(\eta^{3k/2}\) of \cite{KSW}. We also extend \KSW{} categorical picture, representations of \(\Bthree=\PMod(\surf{1}{1})\) built from a modular tensor category, to representations, on fusion-chain block spaces, of a mapping-class subgroup of the \(n\)-punctured torus generated by \(S\), \(T\), and adjacent braidings, with a Verlinde-type dimension formula and categorical \(S\)-, \(T\)-operators. The \(\alg{sl}(2)\) matrix form of \(S\) beyond this abstract construction remains open.
item.dc:creator: A. Zuevsky

item.title: Divergence Liftings and Regular Factorizations for Metric Cotype
item.description: arXiv:2609.32589v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The least regular norm of a factorization of antipodal differences through sign differences on \((\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)^n\) is \(m/2\) when \(4\mid m\). On these tori, when \(2\sqrt n\le m\le4\sqrt n\), normalized divergence equations admit selections with pointwise norm bound \(3/2\), while the least linear lifting norm and global Lipschitz selection constant equal \(\sqrt n/2\). Higher-moment lifting bounds follow from a quoted sharp \(L_1\) inequality.
item.dc:creator: Yue Wang

item.title: The Critical Value for the Beurling-Type Theorem in Weighted Bergman Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.36723v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every $\alpha>1$ we construct a finite set $A\subset\mathbb{D}$ such that the zero-based invariant subspace $I_A$ fails the wandering subspace property. Consequently, the Beurling-type theorem holds on the weighted Bergman space $A^2_\alpha$ if and only if $-1<\alpha\le1$, confirming a conjecture of Shimorin. As a further application, we extend the prescribed-curvature construction of Hedenmalm and Perdomo to all $\alpha>1$, thereby replacing the constant $\alpha_0\approx1.04$ in their result by $1$.
item.dc:creator: Zhaopeng Lin, Shibo Xu, Tao Yu

item.title: Extreme points of the unit balls and isometries of noncommutative quasi-Banach Marcinkiewicz spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.01043v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterize extreme points of the (positive) unit balls of Marcinkiewicz spaces with respect to their natural quasi-norms. Having these results at hand, we show that every positive surjective isometry on a noncommutative Marcinkiewicz space is of elementary form. In particular, a linear mapping on a noncommutative Marcinkiewicz space over an atomic von Neumann algebra with all atoms having the same trace is a positive surjective isometry if and only if it is the restriction of a Jordan $*$-isomorphism which preserves the singular value functions. We also study (not necessarily positive) surjective isometries on weak $L_p$-spaces affiliated a $\sigma$-finite non-atomic von Neumann algebra for $1<p<\infty$, Marcinkiewicz sequence spaces, and weak $\ell_p$ operator ideals, $p>0$, as well as one-parameter groups of isometries on the latter two.
item.dc:creator: Kai Fang, Yi Gao, Jinghao Huang, Fedor Sukochev

item.title: Sharp Asymptotics for $k$-Positivity Shifts under Singular Perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2506.03773v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that, as the Choi matrix of a completely positive perturbation direction approaches a singular limit, the shift required for $k$-positivity can diverge more slowly than that required for complete positivity. For every $k\geq 2$, we construct a $(k-1)$-positive map $\Phi$ and a completely positive map $\Gamma$ on $\mathbb{M}_{k+1}$ with singular Choi matrix $\mathbf{C}_\Gamma$. Regularizing $\Gamma$ by $\Gamma_\varepsilon=\Gamma+\varepsilon\Delta$, where $\Delta(X)=\mathrm{Tr}(X)I$, we determine the least $t\geq 0$ for which $\Phi+t\Gamma_\varepsilon$ is $j$-positive. More precisely, $s_{j,\Gamma_\varepsilon}(\Phi)=0$ for $j<k$, while $s_{k,\Gamma_\varepsilon}(\Phi)\sim c_k\varepsilon^{-(2k+1)/(2k+2)}$ and $s_{k+1,\Gamma_\varepsilon}(\Phi)=\varepsilon^{-1}$. The leading constant $c_k>0$ is determined explicitly. The fractional exponent is obtained through singular-value estimates and an explicit construction of rank-$k$ perturbations of a nilpotent Jordan block.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Kian

item.title: Microlocal defect functionals in VMO: Geometric localisation and applications to highly heterogeneous media
item.description: arXiv:2607.04294v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend the concept of microlocal defect functionals to test functions belonging to the space $\mathrm{L}^\infty\cap\mathrm{VMO}_c$. Following L.~Tartar's remark that an extension of such concepts to $\mathrm{VMO}$ spaces should be possible, we establish a functional-analytic framework for this extension within the $\mathrm{L}^p-\mathrm{L}^q$ setting. Because the topological dual of $\mathrm{VMO}$ is the Hardy space $\mathcal{H}^1$, the resulting object takes the form of an H-distribution rather than a non-negative Radon measure. By assuming strict H\"older conjugate inequalities, we use the John-Nirenberg inequality over localized domains to construct these functionals. We show that the functional acts as a distribution on the inductive limit topology of the test spaces, giving geometric localisation principles for equations with rough $\mathrm{VMO}$ coefficients, that is, coefficients admitting sharp transitions of vanishing mean oscillation. We illustrate the framework in three settings: stratified transport, zero-order non-local cross-phase energies, and sub-critical acoustic scattering in high-contrast media. These differ in the nonlinearity generating the companion sequence but share a common geometric conclusion, since in each case the macroscopic energy defect is confined to the characteristic variety of the underlying flow, being supported where $\sum_j a_j({\bf x})\xi_j=0$.
item.dc:creator: Marin Mi\v{s}ur

item.title: Projection geometry and relaxed quasi-orthogonality for inf-sup stable Galerkin methods
item.description: arXiv:2609.16265v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give an elementary, coordinate-free proof that uniformly inf-sup stable nested Petrov-Galerkin methods on Hilbert spaces satisfy relaxed general quasi-orthogonality. More precisely, for any window of $N$ consecutive levels, the sum of squared Galerkin increments is bounded by the squared error at the beginning of the window times $N^\sigma$, where $\sigma<1$. The exponent $\sigma$ and the prefactor can be chosen explicitly in terms of the uniform projection bound. The proof uses Hilbert-space projection estimates, dyadic iteration, and duality, without relying on matrix factorizations. As a corollary, we obtain explicit growth bounds for finite block-LU factors. In the symmetric indefinite case, the positive and negative spectral splittings of the Galerkin detail spaces yield a characterization of full quasi-orthogonality in terms of uniform boundedness of the associated finite-window sign operators. We also construct a self-adjoint involution and a nested, uniformly inf-sup stable Galerkin sequence for which full general quasi-orthogonality fails. For every $0<\alpha<1$, the construction yields a hierarchy whose finite-window constants have growth of exact order $N^\alpha$, along with an explicit target whose Galerkin increments are not square summable.
item.dc:creator: Tsogtgerel Gantumur

item.title: Regularized barycentric R\'enyi divergences
item.description: arXiv:2609.17517v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Barycentric R\'enyi divergences were introduced in [Mosonyi, Bunth, Vrana, Linear Algebra and its Applications, 2024] as an alternative to standard Kubo-Ando constructions to define multivariate quantum R\'enyi divergences. They are defined via a variational expression and depend on a finite collection of quantum relative entropies $D^{q_x}$. When all the relative entropies are monotone under CPTP maps then so are the corresponding barycentric R\'enyi divergences, and when all the relative entropies are additive then the corresponding barycentric R\'enyi divergences are subadditive under tensor product. Additivity has only been established before for the case where all $D^{q_x}$ are chosen to be the Umegaki relative entropy, which is also the only case where the barycentric R\'enyi divergence (called the minimal one) was known to admit an explicit expression. Here we settle the problem of additivity by showing that for any choice of monotone quantum relative entropies, the regularized barycentric R\'enyi divergence coincides with the minimal barycentric R\'enyi divergence on invertible inputs. This in turn implies that if at least two of the $D^{q_x}$ are strictly larger than the Umegaki relative entropy (in a precise sense), then the resulting barycentric R\'enyi divergence is not even weakly additive.
item.dc:creator: Mil\'an Mosonyi

item.title: Solution to Dixmier's Problem about spectra of C*-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2609.26319v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Dixmier asked in 1967 whether the spectra of simple separable non-type-I $C^*$-algebras all have the same Borel structure. We solve the formulation using ordinary isomorphisms of quotient Borel $\sigma$-algebras by proving that its universal assertion is independent of ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC. Under the continuum hypothesis, all separable non-type-I spectra are measurably isomorphic, without simplicity or unitality assumptions. In the model obtained by iterating Sacks forcing for $\omega_2$ stages with countable supports over a GCH ground model, a fixed simple unital universal spectrum is not measurably isomorphic to the CAR spectrum. Neither consistency direction requires a large cardinal. The Borel-definable formulation, which requires isomorphisms to admit Borel lifts between irreducible representations, has a negative answer in ZFC. For the CAR algebra $A$ and a simple separable exact crossed product $B$ associated to $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$, there is no Borel-definable injection $\widehat B\to\widehat A$. Nevertheless, all separable nuclear non-type-I spectra are Borel-definably isomorphic. We also determine the answer under several choiceless hypotheses. The axiom of determinacy together with dependent choice gives a stronger negative conclusion: the spectrum of $B$ does not even inject as a set into the spectrum of $A$. The symmetric Solovay model gives the same conclusion. Over ZF, a wellordering of the reals of order type $\omega_1$ suffices for a positive answer. The finite-permutation Feferman--Levy model gives another positive answer for the full sigma-generated Borel structures. These comparisons concern the quotient structures themselves, without measure completion.
item.dc:creator: Martino Lupini

item.title: Critical Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities via nonlinear scaling argument
item.description: arXiv:2609.28038v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show functional inequalities with logarithmic weights as a critical case of Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities. Original CKN inequalities have polynomial weights and are shown via scaling argument. In this paper, we develop this argument into it for nonlinear scaling. Our inequalities are generalizations of critical Hardy type inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Megumi Sano, Yerkin Shaimerdenov, Hinako Sugimura

item.title: Deep kernel hedging
item.description: arXiv:2609.34474v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a deep kernel hedging framework that combines the flexibility of deep learning with the structural inductive bias of kernel methods. The hedging functional is restricted to a reproducing kernel Hilbert space whose kernel is parameterized through a neural network embedding of the input features. The framework minimizes a regularized empirical risk under convex loss functions and can accommodate path-dependent information through truncated time-augmented signature features. We derive a generalized representer theorem for the joint hedging problem, reducing the empirical optimization to a finite-dimensional problem. To further reduce the computational cost associated with large kernel matrices, we develop a scalable random Fourier feature approximation and establish convergence guarantees. The random Fourier parameters are sampled once and remain fixed throughout training, while the deep kernel adapts to market data through the learned neural representation. We evaluate the performance of the proposed deep kernel approach on both synthetic and real data and compare it with standard kernel methods and classical deep hedging architectures. Numerical results indicate competitive and robust hedging performance, particularly in low-data regimes, which highlights the benefits of combining expressive neural representations with the inductive bias of kernel methods.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Loup Dupret, Donatien Hainaut, Edouard Motte

item.title: The $L^1$-realization of an elliptic operator with unbounded coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.06659v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish an $L^1$-theory for a class of elliptic operators with unbounded coefficients, extending our earlier semigroup generation results and those of Canale--Rhandi--Tacelli to the endpoint $p=1$. The $L^1$-realization generates a positive analytic $C_0$-semigroup that is compact for every positive time. We characterize the generator domain through weighted estimates and prove consistency with the corresponding $L^p$-semigroups for $1<p<\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Sallah Eddine Boutiah

item.title: Inverse limits of locally convex Lie groupoids
item.description: arXiv:2610.12296v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study strict inverse systems of locally convex Lie groupoids and Lie algebroids. We show that strict inverse limits of Lie algebroids and Lie groupoids inherit natural Lie structures and establish a natural isomorphism of functors $\varprojlim\circ\operatorname{Lie}\cong\operatorname{Lie}\circ\varprojlim$. We then consider inverse systems of integrable Banach-Lie algebroids and their source-simply connected levelwise integrations. We give conditions under which these integrations form a strict inverse system of Lie groupoids and hence their inverse limit integrates the inverse-limit algebroid. Under additional hypotheses on the source-fiber inverse sequence, we describe the obstruction to source-simply connectedness of the resulting integration in terms of the derived inverse limit $\varprojlim^{1}\pi_2$ of the second homotopy groups of the source fibers. We illustrate the theory with several examples: inverse limits of jet groupoids, current groupoids, and gauge groupoids, including the corresponding inverse-limit Atiyah algebroids and a source-simply connected inverse-limit integration arising from the quaternionic Hopf bundle.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Gamal Shaltut
